description: A named group in ECMAScript spelling is refused by the baseline descriptor and by validation here.
descriptor: { descriptor_version: "1.0", root: { type: "object", children: { a: { type: "string", pattern: "(?<n>a)" } } } }

divergence.note: docs/grammars.md §1.2 and §1.3 fix which layer reports each regex construct, and §1.2 states that the two implementations can name the same problem at different layers while the outcome (refused, named, never guessed at) does not differ. This is a documented, intentional divergence from the executed baseline under that rule (SPEC.md amendment 26), not a baseline defect.  The baseline engine cannot compile the ECMAScript named group, so its descriptor compile check refuses the file; this engine compiles it, so the dialect scan names it at validation as the docs §1.2 named-group row prescribes (that row assigns the construct to the validation `pattern` reading precisely because only one engine can compile it). Both refuse the pattern and neither matches data with it; the layer differs, per §1.2.
